title: Complexity of general vertex-connectivity augmentation
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a simple undirected graph \(G\) and a target \(1\leq\lambda<|V(G)|\), computes the minimum number of new edges needed to make \(G\) \(\lambda\)-vertex-connected, when every missing edge is available at unit cost?
why: The question asks whether optimal resilience to vertex failures can be added efficiently when all new links have the same cost and are freely available. These simple input conditions isolate the difficulty of vertex connectivity itself from costly or forbidden links.
status_note: The source explicitly leaves the general unrestricted-link problem open. On 13 September 2026 the May 2026 parameterized result was checked at abstract level; it does not state an unrestricted polynomial-time algorithm. No full resolution was verified and status is source_open.
review_note: Completed individual source and formulation review on 13 September 2026; see statement_review and research/card-completion-20260913/reviews.jsonl.

progress.text: The survey states that unrestricted unweighted general vertex-connectivity augmentation remains open, despite tractability of increasing the target by one and algorithms parameterized by the target.

The new preprint reports time \(2^{O(k\log(k+\lambda))}n^{O(1)}\) with restricted links, where \(k\) is the augmentation budget. This does not remove parameter dependence for the unrestricted-target polynomial-time question.

category_assignment.reason: This asks for classical complexity of graph connectivity augmentation beyond a one-step increase.

importance.reason: Exact unweighted augmentation with all links available isolates the unresolved complexity of general target vertex connectivity.

sentences: Vertex-connectivity measures how many vertex deletions a graph can withstand before disconnecting.
The problem asks for the fewest unit-cost edges that raise this connectivity to an input target.
Every missing edge is available, and the target may grow with the graph.
Known one-increment algorithms and 2026 parameterized progress do not provide polynomial time for every target.
A resolution would clarify the complexity of optimal vertex-failure resilience in the simplest unrestricted augmentation model.

definitions: The graph is finite, undirected and simple, with vertex set \([n]\), \(n\geq2\), and an explicit binary adjacency matrix. The integer \(\lambda\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}\) is part of the input, encoded in binary, and need not be fixed. The available links are exactly \(\binom{V(G)}{2}\setminus E(G)\). An augmentation is any subset \(F\) of these links; its cost is \(|F|\), and no new vertices are permitted. The graph \(G+F\) is \(\lambda\)-vertex-connected if deleting any set of fewer than \(\lambda\) vertices leaves a connected graph. The condition \(\lambda<n\) excludes ambiguous conventions on graphs with too few vertices. The optimum is finite because adding every missing edge produces a complete graph. The algorithm must output the exact minimum integer; equivalently it may decide, for a binary budget \(k\geq0\), whether some augmentation has \(|F|\leq k\). The two tasks are polynomial-time equivalent using the finite \(\binom n2\) budget range. Running time is worst-case bit time bounded by one fixed polynomial in the whole input length, with no exponent or multiplicative nonpolynomial dependence on \(\lambda\). The input graph may have arbitrary initial connectivity; there is no promise that the target increases connectivity by only one.

context_blocks.text: The survey contrasts the polynomial-time unweighted edge-connectivity augmentation problem with the less understood vertex-connectivity version. It explicitly leaves the general unrestricted-link case open while citing a polynomial algorithm for increasing vertex connectivity by one and an algorithm exponential in the target connectivity.

Korhonen and Thorup’s May 2026 preprint reports fixed-parameter tractability in the target connectivity and edge budget even when available links are restricted. This is progress for a more general input model, but its exponential parameter dependence does not provide a polynomial algorithm when the target is unrestricted.

answer_criterion: Provide a complete Lean-checked proof of a deterministic polynomial-time exact algorithm for all target values, or prove that no such algorithm exists. An algorithm polynomial only for fixed target connectivity, a parameterized algorithm exponential in the target or budget, an approximation, or a one-increment result does not meet the guarantee. NP-hardness implies a negative answer only under an explicitly stated P ≠ NP hypothesis.

notes: Recovered the all-missing-links, unit-cost minimum-cardinality variant from Section 3.2 and made target connectivity part of the input.
Defined vertex deletion connectivity, allowable augmentations, graph-size edge cases and decision/optimization equivalence.
Added May 2026 FPT progress without treating parameterized tractability as polynomial time for unrestricted targets.
